text:
sam: Thinking aloud — as we converge the adapter surface across hosted/dedicated/private, can we standardize a handshake that avoids sharing raw long-lived secrets?

ana: absolutely. current proxying during fallbacks is scary from a privilege perspective. What shape do you propose?

sam: two parts: a short-lived `session_token` (scoped, no KMS unwrap) + a compact `manifest` declaring allowed capabilities. token TTL small (10-30s). runtime must not receive any raw KMS blobs.

kumar: operational note: we should make tokens opaque JWTs signed by control plane with `aud:adapter` and a `cap_hash` claim that references the manifest signature. prevents tampering.

liz: failure modes: control plane down -> how do we behave? we can't brick customer traffic for enterprise. suggest policy by customer tier: free -> 503, paid -> try failover region, enterprise -> allow cached read-only for X minutes with audit.

marta: add a `staleness_threshold` to the manifest so runtime can enforce max cached-creds usage. Example manifest: 
```yaml
manifest:
  scope: inference
  allow_rebind: false
  allowed_models: [redwood-v1, redwood-lite]
  cached_stale_after: 120s
  audited: true
```

sam: good. also require `orig_handshake_id` propagated so traces link back to the mint request. we need a standard trace tag.

kumar: agree. also require `orig_handshake_id` be present in `X-Trace-Parent` or `handshake-trace` header to simplify observability.

liz: one more: telemetry/alerts. if runtime uses cached creds > 0s, emit `handshake_cached_credential_used` metric with labels (env, customer_tier, model). create alert if rate > threshold.

marta: security ask: tokens must not allow `kms:Decrypt`. only `infer:InvokeModel` and `cache:Read`. We'll map these ops to internal capability names.

sam: decision for now: prototype minimal handshake fields: `session_token`, `manifest` (signed), `orig_handshake_id`. Not allowing raw secrets. Fallback rules declared by customer tier and manifest `cached_stale_after` value.

kumar: I'll prototype token mint + JWT claims and an integration test that simulates control-plane outage and verifies fallback routing. ETA Tue.

ana: I'll write a short RFC describing manifest shape and the mapping to runtime permissions (including `cached_stale_after` semantics). ETA Thu.

liz: I'll draft the alerting rules and MTTD dashboards. Also propose a live query to find usages of cached creds across clusters. ETA Wed.

deploy-bot: deploy status: handshake-token-service rolled to staging at 7932112700 — integration test failing (403 on token mint). @kumar take a look. :gear:

kumar: looking now. likely policy/role binding change — will revert staging policy and add a regression test.

sam: quick config example (for prototyping):
```yaml
handshake:
  session_token: <opaque-jwt>
  manifest: <signed-yaml-manifest>
  orig_handshake_id: "${uuid()}"
```

marta: also think about minimizing manifest size — runtime RAM matters. use small enums for ops.

sam: true. keep the manifest compact and sign it to avoid runtime parsing complexity.

liz: post-integrations: security review + threat model update. we'll add runtime-side assertion checks to reject any handshake that contains `raw_secret` or `kms_blob`.

sam: ok. next steps recap:
- @kumar: token mint prototype + tests (ETA Tue)
- @ana: draft RFC for manifest -> runtime permission mapping (ETA Thu)
- @liz: telemetry + alerting (ETA Wed)
- @marta: manifest size and enum proposal (ETA Fri)

sam: thanks all — this should significantly reduce accidental privilege exposure during mode handoffs. :thumbsup:
